It’s available in 12-ounce, 20-ounce and 24-ounce sizes, and it comes in options with and without handles — I like the version without the handle to wrap my hands around when I’m cold and to easily place in a cup holder. Topping a standard cup of coffee with warm, foamy milk feels extra special, and you can help your giftee do exactly that at home with this gadget. It turns milk into warm dense foam, warm airy foam, cold foam or standard warm milk. Your loved one will select which option they want and let the milk frother work its magic — then, it automatically stops when it’s done. There are fill lines on the inside of the cup, which comes off of the base to rinse out in the sink. Your giftee can also use the milk frother to make hot chocolate and matcha lattes. Sure, your loved one could brew their espresso shots into the cups their machine came with. But these mini Yeti mugs are an adorable upgrade, says Godio, who uses them while making lattes. Sold as a set of two, they’re made from stainless steel and double-wall vacuum insulated, so they keep espresso extra hot. They also have little handles for your loved one to grip while they sip or pour, and they’re dishwasher-safe and stackable for convenient cleaning and storage. Anyone who buys coffee grinds is missing out on the significantly better flavor of freshly ground beans. Make sure your giftee isn’t one of those people by getting them OXO’s grinder. Its removable hopper holds up to 12 ounces of beans and it’s UV-tinted to keep light out, thus preserving taste. Your loved one can choose from 15 grind settings and 43 micro-adjustments for the stainless steel blades, letting them pick the best option for espresso, Fresh press coffee and more. articles.title: For 30 years, John Ehn built Old Trapper’s Lodge, using life masks of relatives to create faces for fictional Old West figures and “Boot Hill” sculptures
articles.summary: Discover the legacy of John Ehn and his Old Trapper's Lodge, a unique folk-art environment featuring sculptures, life masks, and the fictional Boot Hill Cemetery, all built as a tribute to family and Western folklore.
articles.body: Old Trapper’s Lodge is a collection of concrete sculptures, homemade tombstones and Old West displays that was built by John Ehn at the California motel that he operated with his family. He was a self-taught artist who used life masks of relatives to shape the faces of figures in his fictional Boot Hill Cemetery. The site grew into a large folk-art environment that included characters that were drawn from songs, folktales and stories of the American West. SPACES Archives documents the project as running from about 1951 to 1981, the year Ehn died.A visit to Knott’s Berry Farm started the projectEhn was born Johan Henry Ehn in Michigan in 1897, and worked as a game warden and later trapped alligators and snakes in Florida. He was forced to stop trapping in 1940 because of spinal inflammation, and moved with his family to Southern California and opened a motel. He named the property Old Trapper’s Lodge, and became known for his Western clothing, goatee and other distinctive accessories. The Los Angeles Times reported in 1986 that Ehn’s artistic work began after a 1951 visit to Knott’s Berry Farm, where he hired sculptor Claude Bell to make a large concrete figure of him as a trapper. Ehn watched Bell work for three days, then tried the technique himself.Ehn built the sculptures by first assembling a wire framework and covering it with cement, and he often painted the finished figures in bright colours. His first major series became Boot Hill Cemetery, which is a mock graveyard that is filled with Old West characters and tombstones carrying invented accounts of their deaths. The life masks he made of family members supplied the faces for the statues, and their identities were drawn from the songs and stories he enjoyed. The wider property also housed his Old West Mooseum, which displayed trapping equipment, animal skins, photographs, tools and personal memorabilia.The motel’s sculptures faced relocationThe displays included comic details as well as scenes of violence and frontier folklore, since a tombstone could describe how absurdly a character died, while another exhibit would use an ordinary object as a joke. The 1986 Los Angeles Times report described a display labelled “Pontiac Spring” that contained a coil spring taken from a Pontiac automobile, and Ehn’s motto, “Waste Not Want Not,” also appeared in the way he incorporated odds and ends into the environment. The motel office became a part of the installation, and objects from his trapping years and family life were arranged among historical photographs and other keepsakes.Old Trapper’s Lodge was designated a state historical landmark in 1981 (the year Ehn died at age 84) by California. In 1987, Ehn’s heirs agreed to sell the site, which was acquired for expansion that was connected with Burbank Airport. A July 1988 Los Angeles Times report said that the airport authority planned to demolish the buildings and that the family had been searching for a new home for the sculptures, with the Los Angeles Community College District accepting 20 statues as a gift.Several of Ehn’s larger sculptures were moved to Pierce College in the mid-1980s, where SPACES Archives says they remain available for public viewing, while smaller works are held by the Oakland Museum of California. The original motel and its full collection are gone, but the surviving sculptures stil preserve parts of the project Ehn built over three decades.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Howard Finster developed Paradise Garden from the 1960s onward and, after a reported vision at 59, produced 46,991 religiously themed artworks in Georgia
articles.summary: Explore the inspiring story of Howard Finster, a Georgia preacher who after receiving a divine vision at 59, became a prolific artist creating over 46,000 artworks and establishing the iconic Paradise Garden. Discover the blend of religious themes, recycled materials, and artistic vision that shaped this unique folk art environment.
articles.body: A Georgia preacher and bicycle repairman named Howard Finster was 59 when he said that he received a vision that God was instructing him to create sacred art. He was not trained as an artist, but he began painting in 1976 and went on to produce 46,991 works before his death in October 2001, according to the Paradise Garden Foundation.Finster also built an outdoor art environment called Paradise Garden at his home in Pennville, Georgia, and later incorporated it into Summerville. He filled the property with paintings, concrete sculptures, religious messages, salvaged objects and structures that were assembled from discarded materials, and the garden developed over several decades, with Finster treating the entire site as part of his artistic work. His first painting followed an experience that he described as a face appearing in a dab of white paint on his finger, and interpreted it as a divine instruction to paint sacred art. The episode became important to his account of how he began making art late in life.A garden built around religious messagesFinster initially called the garden a roadside park and museum, and he wanted to display inventions and objects that he considered evidence of human creativity. The garden contains Bible verses that are embedded in concrete, bicycle parts, television tubes, mirrors, bottles, plastic toys and other discarded items. These materials were combined with religious imagery and paintings of historical figures, inventors and public personalities, and some of the objects were collected, while others became part of structures that he built himself.Paradise Garden is described as a two-acre environment by the Smithsonian American Art Museum that Finster began constructing in the 1960s, and its account documents the mixture of religious texts, recycled objects and handmade sculptures across the property. Finster’s paintings produced images of biblical figures alongside politicians, musicians, inventors and celebrities, and he also made plywood cutouts, decorated objects and works on unusual surfaces. He had constant visitors who came to the garden to see the installations and buy his art, and demand grew as his work reached audiences even outside of Georgia.From local preacher to nationally recognised folk artistFinster’s bicycle repair business gave him a practical background in fixing and assembling objects, but he did not begin painting seriously until the vision he described in 1976. His work later entered major museum collections and attracted attention from musicians and popular-culture figures, with the High Museum of Art identifying him as one of the leading self-taught artists of the 20th century and holding a substantial collection of his work, including paintings and pieces that once stood in the garden.Finster’s art made a number of television appearances and had connections with musicians, which helped him reach a wider audience, and his paintings mixed religious subjects with familiar images from American public life, which is a combination that made them different from conventional devotional art. In terms of the volume of paintings produced by him, the Paradise Garden Foundation records 46,991 works completed by the time he died at 84. Finster took help from family members, who assisted him with repetitive tasks such as cutting out patterned shapes and filling background colours. He generally completed the detailed work and added the text himself.The garden after FinsterFinster’s daughter Beverly purchased the garden in 1999, and a nonprofit organisation was later established to preserve it; in 2011, the property was sold to Chattooga County, which arranged for the Paradise Garden Foundation to manage the site. The foundation now maintains the garden and operates it as a public attraction in Summerville, and preserves the outdoor installations, cares for the property and presents Finster’s art to visitors. The garden still remains a physical collection of his paintings, structures and religious messages that was built over decades. Even though Finster’s career began late, his output continued until his final years, and the site he built is still open to visitors and has its original mix of religious art, handmade structures and reused materials.You use AI every day. articles.title: Mark Zuckerberg considered selling $110 million Palo Alto home over 5% billionaire tax; strikes 8-year Meta deal to stay in California as $12 billion tax bill threatens voting control
articles.summary: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg has struck a deal with the company to remain in California after reportedly warning that he could move out of the state if voters
articles.body: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg has struck a deal with the company to remain in California after reportedly warning that he could move out of the state if voters approve a proposed 5% wealth tax on billionaires. According to a Securities and Exchange Commission filing reported by Reuters and California Post, Zuckerberg raised concerns that the proposed levy could leave him facing a multibillion-dollar tax bill and potentially force him to sell shares in Meta.The agreement will allow Zuckerberg to receive a new class of non-voting shares that he can sell to help cover a potential tax liability without significantly affecting his voting control of the company. In return, he has committed to remaining a resident of California, or any other jurisdiction where Meta maintains its corporate headquarters, for eight years, subject to certain exceptions.Why Mark Zuckerberg was considering leaving CaliforniaThe proposed California wealth tax, referred to as Proposition 40 in the reports, would impose a one-time 5% tax on the net worth of billionaires in the state if approved by voters. Zuckerberg, whose estimated net worth is around $240 billion, reportedly warned Meta's board that the measure could expose him to a tax liability running into billions of dollars.According to the filing cited by California Post, Zuckerberg discussed the potential consequences with Meta's directors, including lead independent director Robert M. Kimmitt. He reportedly said the proposed tax could affect his ability to remain a California resident and meet any tax obligation if the measure became law.Most of Zuckerberg's wealth is tied to his approximately 13% ownership stake in Meta, the parent company of Facebook and Instagram. His Class B shares carry enhanced voting rights, allowing him to retain control over the company despite owning a minority of its overall equity.The filing reportedly stated that selling enough of those shares to meet a substantial tax bill could reduce his voting interest to approximately 53%, potentially affecting his control of Meta.Meta's deal with Zuckerberg to protect his voting controlAs reported by Reuters, Meta plans to issue a new class of non-voting Class C common stock in January 2027. The arrangement is intended to provide Zuckerberg with additional liquidity while preserving his voting control over the company.Under the agreement, Zuckerberg can immediately sell 20% of the Class C shares he receives. Those shares represent approximately 10% of his overall economic stake in Meta, according to the Reuters report.The company said the new share structure would also support acquisitions, help retain key employees and provide capital flexibility as Meta continues investing in artificial intelligence.Meta's board reportedly considered it critically important for Zuckerberg to remain in a leadership position as the company faces growing competition and the financial demands of its AI expansion.The filing also indicated that Meta could need to raise hundreds of billions of dollars over several years, beginning as early as autumn 2026, to support its long-term growth plans.Zuckerberg reportedly considered selling his $110 million Palo Alto homeCalifornia Post reported that Zuckerberg had discussed selling his Palo Alto compound, estimated to be worth $110 million, as part of plans to establish residency outside California.According to the publication, he told directors that he would need to begin taking steps by mid-September to establish residency elsewhere by mid-October, ahead of the November 3 election.The report also said Zuckerberg's lawyers sent a letter to a special committee of Meta's board on August 3 seeking changes to his compensation arrangements, including measures to improve his access to liquidity in the event of a substantial tax bill.The discussions subsequently led to negotiations over a revised agreement intended to address his concerns while ensuring his continued leadership at Meta.Under the final arrangement, Zuckerberg has agreed to remain a resident of California, or another jurisdiction where Meta maintains its headquarters, unless significant unforeseen circumstances make it advisable for him to live elsewhere.Sergey Brin and other billionaires oppose California's proposed wealth taxZuckerberg is not the only technology billionaire whose residency and finances have come under scrutiny amid the proposed tax. Google co-founder Sergey Brin has reportedly changed his residency to Nevada and spent substantial sums supporting efforts to defeat the measure.Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt and cryptocurrency entrepreneur Chris Larsen have also contributed significant amounts to campaigns opposing the proposal.The proposed tax has been championed by the Service Employees International Union-United Healthcare Workers West as a way to offset healthcare funding cuts at the federal level.However, the measure faces an uncertain electoral outcome. California Post cited a recent poll showing 46% of respondents supporting the tax and 43% opposing it, suggesting that the proposal had yet to secure majority backing in that survey.Two other ballot measures backed by Brin, identified in the reports as Propositions 41 and 42, could also introduce restrictions affecting the proposed wealth tax if approved by voters.Meta reports revenue growth as AI investment gathers paceThe disclosures about Zuckerberg's negotiations came alongside Meta's second-quarter earnings report, which showed a 26% year-on-year increase in revenue.The company's plans to introduce non-voting shares reflect its efforts to balance Zuckerberg's long-term leadership and voting control with the need to raise capital for future investments.With artificial intelligence reshaping competition across the technology industry, Meta's board has indicated that retaining Zuckerberg at the helm remains a priority as the company prepares for its next phase of growth.You use AI every day. articles.title: For 25 years, Texas factory worker Rufino Loya transformed his wife’s modest El Paso home into a “Sugar House,” covering it with colorful mosaics, shrines, and handmade details
articles.summary: Discover the inspiring story of Rufino Loya Rivas, who spent 25 years transforming his modest home in El Paso into the vibrant 'Sugar House' adorned with colorful mosaics and hand-crafted details. Learn about the artistic journey that turned a simple house into a celebrated landmark.
articles.body: Rufino Loya Rivas bought a modest house in El Paso, Texas, with his wife, Celia, in 1973. He made a promise to transform the property into a place that she would be proud of despite not having any formal training in architecture, art, or construction. He covered the home and its grounds with handmade decorations, painted concrete ornaments, columns, arches, and religious shrines over the next 25 years, and the site became known as La Casa de Azúcar, or the Sugar House, according to the SPACES Archives.Loya was sewing pockets into denim jeans at El Paso’s Levi Strauss manufacturing plant before retiring in 1995. He built the decorations in his spare time and used inexpensive materials because stonework and specialised carving tools were not within his budget. He used cups, bowls and other kitchen containers as moulds for the shapes that he made from cement and plaster. The main construction period ran from 1973 to 1998, and Loya continued to repaint and repair parts of the property after that, and was able to maintain the artwork around the house and its boundary walls.How an ordinary house acquired its elaborate exteriorLoya began with a decorated archway over the path to the front door with rocks and painted plaster flowers, then expanded the project to flowerpot bases, window surrounds, fences and freestanding columns, which eventually extended across much of the property. He moulded cement into flowers, leaves, spheres and beads, with some pieces attached to the house itself, while others became part of pillars and walls in the yard. He also cut aluminium cans into thin flower shapes, fastening the pieces together with bottle caps.The design was inspired by the decorative stonework and religious ornamentation that Loya remembered from Catholic churches in Mexico, and the result was an extensive collection of handmade objects and structures around the original house. According to Roadside America’s account of the property, Loya used kitchen containers to cast repeated decorative patterns and incorporated them into the yard’s structures.Religious shrines became a major part of the propertyLoya built shrines that were dedicated to the Sacred Heart of Jesus, the Virgin of Guadalupe, Saint Francis of Assisi and other Catholic figures, with intricate painted statues, angels and decorative concrete work. One large altar was decorated with angels and small cherub figures and took more than 600 hours to complete, according to the SPACES Archives, while a separate shrine that was dedicated to the Virgin of Guadalupe took almost a year to construct. Loya also included memorial structures as a tribute to people killed in the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks.Small signs around the property carry messages in English and Spanish, with one reading, “This house is a little piece of Mexico,” which reflects Loya’s connection to his birthplace and his life in El Paso. The house got its nickname because of its elaborate ornamentation, with passersby thinking that the layered decorations resembled a cake covered in sugar frosting. Loya accepted the comparison and stated that the property was a tribute to his adopted city and its residents.The house remains a private residenceThe Sugar House is at 4301 Leavell Avenue in El Paso, and its decorations can be seen from the street, but the property is privately owned and the fenced area is not open for unrestricted entry. Photographs documented the property in 2008 and again in 2018, with the intention of preserving views of the house, its decorated walls and its shrines. The archive’s record also notes that Loya died on August 13, 2022, and the future of the site was uncertain.The Sugar House’s main period of construction ended in 1998, but its structures are still a record of the work that was carried out by Loya over a quarter-century. The house and its exterior artwork are still visible from the surrounding street, although visitors should not enter the private grounds without permission.You use AI every day. articles.title: WHO warns ‘more complex’ Ebola outbreak now present in 3 African countries
articles.summary: Health officials are investigating where Nigeria’s first patient, confirmed this week, was infected.
articles.body:
The World Health Organization (WHO) says the Ebola outbreak that emerged in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is growing more “complex”, with cases now present in countries in East and West Africa.

This comes as health authorities investigate where Nigeria’s first case , which was confirmed this week, originated, raising questions about whether the patient crossed paths with Kenya’s first patient at a Ugandan airport.

“We are facing a more complex outbreak landscape,” Mohamed Janabi, regional director for WHO in Africa, told an online media briefing on Thursday.

Nigeria reported its first case of the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola on Tuesday, becoming the fourth ⁠African country and the most populous yet to be affected by an outbreak that was announced in DRC in mid-May and has since killed more than 4,000 people there.

Kenya, DRC and Nigeria all have active or recent cases of the Bundibugyo strain, while Uganda had cases earlier in the year but has since been declared Ebola-free.

The Nigeria patient is the Ugandan-born wife of a Swiss diplomat based in Abuja. Authorities in Uganda said she had travelled to eastern DRC before transiting through Uganda. But the WHO and Africa’s top health agency said on ⁠Thursday they had not received confirmed information that the woman travelled to the DRC.

A Swiss government statement to the Reuters news agency also said the patient is believed to have contracted the disease while travelling in Uganda.

Wessam Mankoula, the head of Emergency Preparedness and Response at the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC), said on Thursday that both the first Nigerian case and the first Kenyan case had left Entebbe on October 3, and that a possible encounter between them was under investigation.

Ugandan authorities rejected the suggestion that she was infected in the country. Government spokesman Alan Kasujja told the AFP news agency that it was “preposterous” to link Uganda to the case simply because she had holidayed there.

However, Mankoula said there was no validated information that she had been to DRC, and Jean Kaseya, the Africa CDC director general, said the same. Pavel Ursu, the WHO representative in Nigeria, said the information given to the organisation included no travel outside Uganda.

Patrick Otim, a WHO emergency response manager, said on Thursday the source of her infection was still unknown as health authorities were working to piece together her travel history.

Investigators were looking at which Abuja health facilities she visited between the onset of symptoms and her hospitalisation 48 hours later, he added.

Kenya’s Ministry of Health confirmed its first case earlier this month and had reported eight more since. Patrick Amoth, the Health Ministry’s director-general, said officials had traced all 135 contacts of the first case.

Nigeria is now tracing 44 contacts, and Mankoula said more had since been identified but did not give a new number.

The current outbreak is the deadliest in DRC’s history, according to the country’s health authorities. It has killed more than 4,000 people out of more than 9,000 confirmed cases since May.

Neighbouring Uganda recorded 20 confirmed cases, including 15 imported from the DRC, and two deaths, before it was declared Ebola-free in August.

The Africa CDC has warned of an “extremely serious threat”, with the fatality rate in DRC approaching 50 percent.

articles.title: White evangelical support for Trump slips but still strong as midterms near
articles.summary: Poll finds white evangelicals still outpace other demographic groups in supporting Trump, as he rallies right-wing base.
articles.body:
United States President Donald Trump’s support among white evangelical Protestant voters remains strong but has slipped since he retook office in January 2025, according to a new poll.

A survey released this month by the news agency Reuters and research firm Ipsos found that Trump’s support among the group had tumbled to 63 percent, down from 77 percent at the time of his second inauguration.

The shift comes as Trump’s approval rating drops to an all-time low of 31 percent.

White evangelicals are considered a key Republican demographic, and the decline could prove significant during the midterm elections on November 3, when the right-wing party will seek to defend its majorities in Congress.

Democrats remain widely favoured to take control of the US House of Representatives in the election. Their chances of flipping the Senate too are increasing amid widespread discontent over affordability and the US-Israeli war on Iran.

But experts say Republicans are counting on their base to counter signs of a Democratic surge at the polls.

On Wednesday, Trump campaigned in South Carolina, located in the southern “Bible Belt”, where exit polls found six in 10 Republican voters were white evangelicals in the 2024 presidential primary.

Trump carried the state by nearly 18 percentage points in the 2024 presidential election, but polls have shown Republican Senate candidate Darline Graham holding only a narrow lead over Democratic challenger Annie Andrews just two weeks ahead of the midterm vote.

As with many of his campaign appearances, Trump focused his South Carolina speech on several social issues that resonate with conservative Christians, including policies related to transgender people. During the rally, he referred to Andrews with an anti-transgender slur.

“She’s a fanatical transgender activist,” Trump said at a different point in his speech, despite Andrews skewing moderate on the issue within the Democratic Party. “How the hell do you run in South Carolina? Am I in a different state?”

Long a key demographic in Trump’s coalition, white evangelicals accounted for nearly a third of Trump’s winning coalition in 2024, according ⁠to a Public Religion Research Institute (PRRI) survey and a validated-voter analysis by the nonpartisan Pew Research Center.

The US president has been able to maintain support from key evangelical leaders despite a series of scandals at odds with the conservative values they espouse. Trump has faced allegations of sexual misconduct and extramarital affairs, which he denies.

All told, about 80 percent of white evangelical voters cast their ballots for Trump in the 2024 general election. The demographic makes up about 13 percent of the overall US population.

Beyond states like South Carolina, evangelicals in the Midwestern states of Iowa and Kansas, as well as the Southern state of Texas, could be key to the Republican Party maintaining its hold on the US Senate.

Christian faith leaders are challenging Republicans in several top races, including Adam Hamilton, a United Methodist Church pastor, in Kansas, and James Talarico, a Presbyterian seminarian, in Texas.

Both Hamilton and Talarico represent mainline Protestant denominations, not evangelical ones.

White evangelicals’ voter trends are distinct from other evangelical groups. For example, Black Protestant evangelicals, a vanguard of the US civil rights movement, have remained a key Democratic voting bloc.

Still, support for Trump among evangelicals remains strong compared with other demographic groups.

It remains unclear if shifting attitudes towards Trump would affect conservative turnout during the midterm elections, in which the US president is not on the ballot.

The Reuters news agency noted that white evangelicals were the only demographic it tracks that surpassed 60 percent support for Trump in the final stretch of the midterms.

The drop in support among the group was less pronounced than for Trump’s overall approval rating, tumbling 14 percentage points compared with a 16-point decline among Americans overall.

articles.title: US actor Tom Skerritt, who starred in Picket Fences, Mash and Alien, dies aged 93
articles.summary: The actor died on Wednesday of natural causes, his family said.
articles.body:
US actor Tom Skerritt, who starred in the TV series Picket Fences and the films Alien and Top Gun, has died aged 93, his family says.

Skerritt died on Wednesday of natural causes, his family said: "While the world knew Tom through his remarkable acting career, we knew him for his humour, curiosity, wisdom, generosity, and the love he brought into our lives."

In a six-decade career, he took on film and TV roles, appearing in the film Mash, A River Runs Through It and Ted. He also co-founded TheFilmSchool in Seattle to support next-generation filmmakers and storytellers.

His family said he will be remembered "for his belief that stories can help people heal, find purpose, and create change".

The moustachioed star of several 20th century hit films was born in 1933 in Detroit, Michigan, and served in the US Air Force before pursuing an acting career that boasted several military roles.

He made his film debut in 1962 alongside a young Robert Redford ​in War Hunt and years later re-teamed with Redford in the 1992 period drama A River Runs Through It, which starred Brad Pitt.

Skerritt's breakthrough role came when he played US army surgeon Duke Forrest in the 1970 Korean War comedy Mash, which also starred Donald Sutherland, Elliott Gould and Sally Kellerman.

The hit film, which was released amid unrest over the Vietnam War, was nominated for five Academy Awards and was adapted for television two years later.

He also starred alongside Sigourney Weaver in the 1979 sci-fi film Alien, which earned two Oscar nominations, and led to three sequels and several crossover projects.

"It is spontaneity and impulse ​that make the difference, and that is ⁠what I felt we had with 'Alien,'" Skerritt said in a 2019 interview, according to Reuters news agency.

"Every one of us had that immediate rapport with each other."

Skerritt said that one of the things he liked most when he first read the script was that "the woman becomes a hero", referring to Weaver's character, Ripley.

During his career, he starred opposite several strong female leads.

He appeared with Shirley MacLaine in the 1977 film Turning Point and played Sally Field's husband in 1989's Steel Magnolias.

As Commander Mike "Viper" Metcalf in the 1986 classic Top Gun, the versatile actor appeared alongside a young Tom Cruise in the blockbuster.

On television, he won an Emmy Award in 1993 for his role as Sheriff Jimmy Brock in David E Kelley's drama Picket Fences.

The quirky procedural's ensemble cast was nominated for SAG Awards in 1995 and 1996, and he received a nod for male actor in a drama series in 1995.

Picket Fences star Lauren Holly, who played Skerritt's deputy on Picket Fences, described him in a tribute as "our leader".

"His example made those years such a joy and we all loved and respected him so much," Holly wrote, adding: "He cared deeply for his family-both the one at home and the one at work. He cared deeply for his planet, and all of its inhabitants. He had a huge impact on my life, and so many memories I have of him include sharing fits of crippling laughter."

Skerritt also had guest roles on the small screen in The West Wing, Madam Secretary, Law & Order: SVU and Huff. He reteamed with Field as the family patriarch, William Walker, in the drama Brothers & Sisters from 2007-09.

He had a six-episode stint on Cheers playing Rebecca Howe's crush-worthy boss Evan Drake.

In a statement, Skerritt's family said that he leaves behind a "legacy that reaches far beyond the screen".

A deep believer in the power of storytelling, Skerritt helped found the TheFilmSchool in Seattle and co-founded the Red Badge Project, which helps veterans work through PTSD, anxiety and depression by writing and sharing their experiences.

Inspired in part by his experience filming A River Runs Through It, he also believed in protecting the natural world.

He created the documentary series Reflections of the River about America's rivers and supported river conservation.

Skerrit is survived by his third wife Julie, five children and several grandchildren.

articles.title: Tourist dangles 23 stories above busy street in 'reckless' daredevil stunt
articles.summary: A Belgian tourist's parachute became snagged on Auckland's Hotel Indigo during a BASE jump, leaving him dangling 23 stories above a New Zealand street and requiring an emergency rescue.
articles.body: A spine-tingling rescue unfolded in New Zealand this week after a tourist's parachute became snagged on a luxury hotel, leaving the man dangling 23 stories above a busy street before his eventual arrest. The tourist, a Belgian national, was attempting to BASE jump from the 27th floor of Auckland's Hotel Indigo when his parachute became caught on the building's exterior. BASE jumping is an extreme sport that involves parachuting from fixed objects, including buildings, bridges and cliffs. MAN FIGHTS FOR HIS LIFE AFTER TRAGIC CLIFF JUMP INTO WATER AT VACATION HOT SPOT The incident took place at around 10:42 p.m. Tuesday night, police said. The 22-year-old man has since been charged and is scheduled to appear in Auckland District Court on Oct. 27, according to police. The rescue came at a steep cost, with firefighters forced to smash a glass panel worth about $20,000 New Zealand dollars (about $11,400 USD) to reach the stranded tourist. "Fire and Emergency New Zealand were able to free the man. However, the building suffered damage to the exterior, and guests staying at the hotel had their evening disrupted due to the event," Inspector Grae Anderson, the area commander of Auckland City, said in a press release. Police reported that the tourist was not injured and did not require medical treatment. Anderson said investigators believe the tourist was the same person who filmed himself BASE jumping from another Auckland building in September that was under construction. articles.title: Florida cop Brian Louis Sguros found 71-year-old Dennis West dead in his home in 2022, took over the property weeks after his death and impersonated him while spending over $214,000 on renovations, police say
articles.summary: A Florida police officer has been arrested after investigators accused him of unlawfully taking over the home of a man who died in 2022, spending more
articles.body: A Florida police officer has been arrested after investigators accused him of unlawfully taking over the home of a man who died in 2022, spending more than $214,000 renovating the property and using the deceased man’s personal information to obtain permits.Brian Louis Sguros, 35, an officer with the Lauderhill Police Department, was arrested on Tuesday on multiple felony charges following an investigation into his alleged takeover of Dennis West’s home in Florida. According to the Broward County Sheriff’s Office and court documents, Sguros was among the officers who responded to a welfare check at West’s residence on July 11, 2022, when the 71-year-old was found dead inside.The case came to light after a real estate company purchased the property from West’s heirs and subsequently encountered Sguros, who allegedly sought reimbursement for repairs and improvements he claimed to have made.Florida police officer accused of taking over deceased man’s homeAccording to the Broward County Sheriff’s Office, Sguros responded to the welfare check at West’s home on July 11, 2022. The medical examiner later determined that West had died of natural causes due to arteriosclerotic cardiovascular disease, according to the arrest affidavit.Investigators allege that Sguros presented himself to the medical examiner’s office as West’s friend and claimed that the deceased man had no living relatives. Authorities said there was no indication that Sguros knew West and that the claim about his family was untrue.Paperwork filed by Sguros reportedly indicated that he took possession of the property in August 2022, just weeks after West’s death.From August 2022 until February 2025, he allegedly cleaned, repaired and renovated the home. According to the arrest affidavit, Sguros claimed to have spent at least $214,000 of his own money on the property while also paying taxes and utility bills in West’s name.In civil filings, Sguros maintained that he had taken over the home because it was hazardous and he wanted to prevent criminal activity and squatters from occupying it.Investigators allege officer used dead man’s personal informationThe investigation allegedly uncovered searches conducted by Sguros on law enforcement databases using his work computer. According to the arrest affidavit, the searches accessed West’s driver’s licence record and revealed personal information, including his address, date of birth and Social Security number.Authorities allege that Sguros subsequently used West’s identity to obtain a permit from the city of Lauderhill to carry out repairs at the property. Investigators also accused him of forging West’s signature on the permit application, which reportedly listed Sguros’ own telephone number.The affidavit further detailed work carried out at the home in 2024, when a contractor was hired to replace exterior doors and windows. A project manager told police that he did not know West was dead at the time and recalled Sguros telling him that West was “unavailable”.The alleged use of the deceased man’s identity is among the central elements of the criminal investigation.Real estate company uncovers alleged property takeoverThe situation came to light after a real estate company purchased the property from West’s heirs. According to the arrest affidavit, the company obtained lawful possession of the home through probate proceedings in autumn 2025.However, when an employee attempted to take possession of the property, they encountered Sguros. He eventually surrendered the keys before the company’s attorney filed an unlawful detainer action, a legal process used to recover possession of property.Despite handing over the keys, Sguros allegedly demanded reimbursement for the repairs and improvements he claimed to have made.In February, he filed a complaint against the real estate company, detailing how he said he had discovered West inside the home while on duty and subsequently began cleaning, securing and investing in the property.According to the arrest affidavit, however, his records did not establish that he had acquired the home through a purchase, lease, deed, probate appointment or any relationship with West’s heirs.Sguros sought more than $200,000 in the civil litigation for the work he claimed to have carried out, the affidavit stated.In May, an attorney representing the real estate company submitted a complaint to the Lauderhill Police Department, leading to further scrutiny of the case.Brian Louis Sguros faces multiple felony chargesSguros was arrested on Tuesday and faces charges including official misconduct, criminal use of a deceased person’s identification, criminal use of personal identification information, an offence against a computer user and unlawful use of a two-way communications device.According to NBC South Florida, Sguros appeared in court on Wednesday and was ordered held on a $25,000 bond. Following his arrest, he was placed on administrative leave without pay by the Lauderhill Police Department.It was not immediately clear whether Sguros had retained an attorney who could comment on the allegations.The charges stem from investigators’ allegations concerning the property and the use of West’s personal information. The accusations have not, by themselves, established guilt in court.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Omagh: 'Difficult decision' to close Samaritans branch after more than 50 years
articles.summary: "Sadly, and due to circumstances beyond anyone's control, the difficult decision was reached to close the branch," they charity says.
articles.body:
An elected representative has called for "answers" after the closure of the Omagh, County Tyrone, branch of the Samaritans charity.

Founded in 1953, the Samaritans focus on preventing suicides by connecting trained volunteers with people who are struggling. The charity estimates it answers a call for help every 10 seconds.

The Omagh branch, which had been part of the community for more than 50 years, had about 20 'active' volunteers, the charity said.

In a statement, the charity said "due to circumstances beyond anyone's control" a "difficult decision" was reached to close the branch.

Last year, the BBC learned that dozens of branches had voiced concerns over the plan to close more than 100 branches across the UK and Ireland.

At the time, the Samaritans said that having more than 200 branches "is not sustainable" and hindered them from providing the best service.

On Thursday, a Samaritans spokesperson told BBC News NI the closure of the branch "is not related to Samaritans future-proofing programme, which is not currently looking at services in Northern Ireland".

Samaritans of Omagh had not been open for face-to-face support with members of the public since March 2020, when all branches reduced services due to Covid-19 restrictions.

BBC News NI spoke to a former Omagh team member, who shared the volunteers' concerns about their future.

The branch covered counties Fermanagh and Tyrone, with volunteers making lengthy journeys for shifts, and they they said volunteers are conscious that the distance between other branches in Northern Ireland may be unattainable.

It is understood that the news of the closure came via email and those without email addresses were left unaware.

Speaking to BBC News NI, Sinn Féin councillor Barry McElduff said he intends to propose an "informal meeting" between Fermanagh and Omagh District Council and the charity "to explore the issues which have arisen and contributed to the closure".

"There is a lot of uncertainty as to the reasons that this has happened. We need answers," he said.

"There are a significant number of volunteers in the Omagh area, as I understand it, and there is a great need for this service."

A spokesperson for the charity said the Omagh branch "has been a valued part of Samaritans for more than 50 years" and they "recognise the contribution made" by successive trustees, directors, leaders and all volunteers.

"Sadly, and due to circumstances beyond anyone's control, the difficult decision was reached to close the branch," they said.

"Samaritans operates a national listening service, so people in Tyrone and across Northern Ireland will be unaffected and will remain able to access help from Samaritans at any time, day or night, 365 days a year on 116 123 or at samaritans.org.

"All volunteers in the branch have been offered support, as well as receiving one to one phone calls offering support and guidance around relocation. Support meetings have also been offered.

"Some volunteers have already begun the process of transferring to other locations."

The charity said any proceeds from future property sales will be reinvested into running Samaritans services across the UK and Ireland.

If you have been affected by any of the issues raised in this story, information and support can be found at the BBC's Action Line .

articles.title: Thousands gather at final student-led rally ahead of Serbia election
articles.summary: The student movement aims to end Vucic’s 14 years of rule at Sunday’s vote, as he holds a rival rally across town.
articles.body:
Tens of thousands of supporters of Serbia’s student-led opposition movement have gathered in central Belgrade for their final rally ahead of a parliamentary election in which they hope to oust veteran leader Aleksandar Vucic’s party.

The crowds filled the capital on Thursday, as Vucic held a rival rally at a sports hall across town.

Waving “students are winning” flags and blowing whistles, the marchers converged on Slavija Square, the site of some of the movement’s biggest protests.

Sunday’s vote is seen as a chance to end Vucic’s longtime rule.

“Really, for the first time in my life, I believe that it is possible,” said Marija Nedeljkovic Radic, 47, who said young people had given her hope of “ a normal country “.

The vote follows nearly two years of student-led protests triggered by the 2024 collapse of a canopy at a newly renovated railway station in Novi Sad that killed 16 people.

The Student List, a leaderless movement of student-backed candidates, is seeking to unseat Vucic’s right-wing populist Serbian Progressive Party (SNS), which has been in power for more than 14 years.

It is running 250 candidates for the 250-seat parliament, many of them academics or political outsiders, on a platform centred on fighting corruption.

“We are putting an end to 14 years of humiliation, chaos and betrayal, and to decades of putting personal and party interests above yours,” university professor Jugoslav Gasic, one of the candidates on the Student List, told the crowd in Belgrade, who chanted “Victory, victory!”

“You deserve better, and we know how to deliver it. Students are winning!”

The railway disaster, widely blamed on corruption , triggered some of Serbia’s largest demonstrations since the fall of Slobodan Milosevic in 2000, and demands for transparency grew into calls for an early election.

Over the week, students marched for days across the country, including rural areas that are Vucic’s strongholds.

Vucic, who resigned the presidency in September to run for prime minister, called the snap election last month. He has accused the movement of being a foreign-funded coup attempt.

“Let us go out and defeat them! Defeat them decisively!” he told supporters on Thursday.

Serbia lacks reliable independent polling. But political scientist Dusan Vucicevic told the AFP news agency he expected the students to win more than 40 percent of the vote, far more than any opposition list since the SNS took power in 2012.

The Associated Press news agency reported that polls suggested a close race between the two sides, raising fears of incidents if both claim victory.

Twenty-four Serbian civil society groups warned this week that conditions for “free and fair elections” were lacking, and a monitoring group cited more than 100 violent incidents during the campaign.

On Wednesday, prosecutors questioned six people arrested on suspicion of plotting “violence, riots and attacks” on election day.

articles.title: Karoline Leavitt says her previous job was obviously not for Katie Zacharia who survived as press secretary for 5 days
articles.summary: Karoline Leavitt said the job that she left was obviously not meant for Katie Zacharia who had to leave the role in five says because it is a tough job.
articles.body: Karoline Leavitt said the job that she left was obviously not meant for Katie Zacharia who had to leave the role in five says because it is a tough job. “Look, White House press secretary is a tough job. I know that because I did it,” Leavitt said in a Thursday interview with Fox News Digital.“Many people say it’s one of the hardest jobs in politics. It takes a lot of preparation. Sometimes you don’t know how someone will perform until they go out there,” she said. “As the president said, we wish Katie the best. The job obviously was not for her.”Leavitt said she had been advising the president in his search for Zacharia's replacement and outlined the five qualities a press secretary needs: tough, smart, loyal, who understands Trump's policies, and who can put up a fight.“I do obviously talk to him about what the job entails, and he knows it very well. Nobody understands the press better than Donald Trump. He knows that he needs someone who is tough, who is smart, who understands his policies, who is loyal and can go out there and put up a fight,” she said.Leavitt left the role after the birth of her second child though she is not taking a break from work at all. From November 1, she would be joining Fox News as an on-air contributor, providing political analysis and commentary.Leavitt served as President Donald Trump's first press secretary during his second term and made a record as the youngest person in the role. She said she used to prepare a lot before her press conferences, and especially for her first press conference. "I poured myself into my preparation. I read, I studied, I talked to every Cabinet member, I talked to the president. I just absorbed as much information as this noggin up here could," Leavitt said.While Zacharia's first press conference was widely panned as unimpressive, the nail in the coffin was the credibility of her degree. articles.title: Will decide on any notice to remove CEC according to rules: Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Amid speculation that the opposition may make a fresh move for the removal of CEC Gyanesh Kumar, Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla Thursday said he
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Amid speculation that the opposition may make a fresh move for the removal of CEC Gyanesh Kumar, Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla Thursday said he would take a decision according to rules and procedures when he receives such a notice.Both the Lok Sabha Speaker and the Rajya Sabha chairman had rejected previous notices from the opposition, saying their allegations “do not prima facie meet the high constitutional bar for removal proceedings”.Birla noted the process for removal of the chief election commissioner was the same as for removing a Supreme Court judge.Amid protests from the opposition and activist groups, Birla also emphasised India’s democratic strength, saying democracy was ingrained in the country’s fabric. “Whatever happens in the world has an impact in India. It will be our effort that the world benefits from our system of dialogue and free speech,” he said ahead of India hosting the 12th Brics parliamentary forum on Oct 26-27. PM Modi will interact with the delegates at the event.Birla was replying to a question about ongoing protests but parried further queries regarding the politics around the agitation, which is critical of EC and govt, saying these should be directed to political parties.With Congress criticising govt for not proroguing Parliament’s monsoon session, which was adjourned indefinitely on Aug 13, Birla said Article 85 of the Constitution comprehensively covers the issue and noted there were past instances of a session not being prorogued for a longer period. The Speaker had no role in this, he added.Congress has said the decision to not prorogue the session, which will allow govt to reconvene Parliament at a short notice, was deliberate as NDA was trying to cobble together a two-thirds majority to revive its constitutional amendment bill to roll out women’s reservation in Lok Sabha and state assemblies from 2029 with delimitation to increase the strength of the lower House by nearly 50%.Official sources said a Parliament session, when not prorogued, could be summoned at a three-day notice.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Movie glorifies violence, generalises graft in medical field: IMA
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Indian Medical Association has written to I&B ministry to urgently review the promotional content of Sunny Deol-starrer ‘Suryaa – Ant Se
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Indian Medical Association has written to I&B ministry to urgently review the promotional content of Sunny Deol-starrer ‘Suryaa – Ant Se Aarambh Tak’, alleging that it generalises corruption in the medical profession and depicts violence against healthcare workers in ways that could erode public trust and put doctors’ safety at risk.In a letter, dated Oct 22, to I&B minister Ashwini Vaishnaw, IMA national president Dr Anilkumar J Nayak sought an impartial review of the promo video for the upcoming film and appropriate corrective measures from its makers. It also called for a ban or other action if justified under applicable law. The letter was also copied to the Union health and home ministries and the chairperson of National Medical Commission.IMA flagged what it described as the risk of portraying corruption and unethical practices as representative of the medical fraternity. While stressing that individual wrongdoing must be investigated and punished, it said the actions of a few should not tarnish the reputation of doctors as a community.It expressed concern over scenes depicting physical assaults on doctors, nurses and hospital staff, particularly when such acts appear heroic or justified. It warned that such portrayals could normalise violence against healthcare professionals, who already face safety challenges in hospitals.The letter said such depictions could fuel mistrust between patients and doctors, weakening the cooperation essential for treatment and healthcare delivery. It also warned that such negative portrayals could demoralise medical students and discourage young people from entering the profession.IMA said that while it respected freedom of creative expression, the same should be exercised responsibly when healthcare worker safety and public confidence in essential services are at stake.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Centre flags data gap, regulatory hurdles in curbing hospital mark-ups
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Amid SC’s scrutiny of hospitals charging patients steep mark-ups on medicines and consumables, govt officials have flagged gaps in data and
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Amid SC’s scrutiny of hospitals charging patients steep mark-ups on medicines and consumables, govt officials have flagged gaps in data and regulatory hurdles in extending price controls to hospital supplies, saying the Centre first needs to establish the extent of margins before considering intervention.The Union govt has told the SC in its affidavit that margins on hospital consumables can range from 100% to 1,000% or more, highlighting concerns over the high mark-ups patients often face on supplies used during treatment. However, a senior official told TOI that the govt does not have the data needed to assess margins across hospital supplies and determine whether wider controls are warranted.“We first need to get the data and then examine whether there is a margin and a need to control it,” another senior official said, explaining that the purchase price of medicines and consumables would need to be compared with what hospitals charge patients before deciding on any intervention.Centre fixes ceiling prices for scheduled medicines and has limited annual price increases for non-scheduled drugs up to 10%. It has decided to cap trade margins on certain anti-cancer medicines at 30% of MRP. Extending similar controls to other medicines and hospital consumables, officials said, would require analysis and consultation.A health ministry official, however, raised doubts about how far the govt could regulate hospital billing, saying hospitals, with health being a state subject and governed by the Clinical Establishments Act or other laws enacted by state govts.. The Centre’s role, the official said, is largely confined to drug-price regulation through the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority.Regulating individual components of hospital bills would be difficult, the official said, pointing out that hospitals charge package rates without providing detailed itemised bills. Restricting charges on consumables could lead profitconscious hospitals to raise other fees, including surgeons’ charges, the official argued.The official also disputed the blanket use of the term “overcharging” when hospitals bill patients at the MRP, saying there is no general legal requirement to offer discounts below the printed price. They cited delayed reimbursements from insurance firms and govt health schemes as financial pressures on hospitals that would need to be factored in while deciding any broader intervention.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: A 7.0 earthquake hits China’s Tibet, killing 16 and injuring 32
articles.summary: BEIJING — A magnitude 7 earthquake hit China’s Tibet region on Thursday evening, killing at least 16 people, injuring 32 and collapsing hundreds of homes in the northern regional city of Nagqu, official media said.
articles.body: BEIJING — A magnitude 7 earthquake hit China’s Tibet region on Thursday evening, killing at least 16 people, injuring 32 and collapsing hundreds of homes in the northern regional city of Nagqu, official media said. Search and rescue efforts continued following the collapse of at least 339 homes, the Nagqu media office said, citing city government officials. Among the injured, 11 people were in serious condition and the other 21 sustained minor injuries, the media office said. Rescue teams from police and fire departments were building tents to house people displaced by the quake. It was the biggest earthquake in the region in the last five years, China’s national broadcaster CCTV said. The U.S. Geological Survey said the quake occurred at 10:33 p.m. local time, with its epicenter 191 kilometers (119 miles) east-northeast of Nagqu, in a sparsely populated, high-altitude area of northern Tibet. It put the earthquake’s depth at 18 kilometers (11 miles). China’s official Xinhua News Agency cited the China Earthquake Networks Center as putting the depth at 10 kilometers (6.2 miles). Nagqu is more than 300 kilometers (186 miles) north of Tibet’s capital, Lhasa.

articles.title: Govt plans colour-coded driving licence for Indians, foreigners
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: In a first, govt has proposed mentioning the nationality of driving licence holders on DLs and introducing separate colour schemes for Indian
articles.body: NEW DELHI: In a first, govt has proposed mentioning the nationality of driving licence holders on DLs and introducing separate colour schemes for Indian andforeign nationals as well as doing away with affidavits sworn before an executive magistrate or notary as proof of age and address, which has the potential of being misused.Life insurance policies, too, would no longer be accepted as proof. Proposing sweeping changes to the driving licence (DL) regime under Motor Vehicles Rules, the road transport ministry Wednesday issued a draft notification to raise the pass mark for the online safe-driving tutorial assessment from the current 60% to 75%.It has also proposed making it mandatory for licences to carry the holder’s blood group, mobile number and emergency contact details. The ministry has proposed waiving fees for specified DL services, including changes to address, name and contact number, if applicants avail themselves of these services through online Aadhaar authentication.At present, if an applicant cannot produce any of the 12 listed documents, the licencing authority “may accept an affidavit sworn before an executive magistrate, judicial magistrate or notary public as proof of age and address”. Anil Chhikara, an expert in motor vehicle licencing, said, “The use of simple affidavits is being phased out after miscreants used them to register false addresses and dates of birth. Applicants must now provide verifiable documents.”Under the draft, the ministry has listed separate sets of documents for proof of address, age and identity. Address proofs include Aadhaar card, Electoral Photo Identity Card, e-ration card, electricity or gas bills for the preceding three months, and proof of legal presence for foreign nationals. Acceptable age proofs include passports, school board mark sheets, birth certificates and identity cards issued by govt departments. Aadhaar, passports, e-ration cards and PAN have been listed as acceptable identity proofs.The proposed changes aim to curb the submission of false documents, tighten assessment requirements and make licence-related services more accessible. They also seek to streamline online DL services and set timelines for processing applications to change licence particulars.Under the proposal, the safe-driving tutorial would have to last at least 30 minutes, while the higher qualifying score of 75% is intended to make the assessment more stringent. Licencing authorities would have to approve or reject online applications to change DL particulars, including name and address, within 15 days, giving reasons for rejection.An application for a change of address that remains undecided for 30 days would be deemed approved. The draft also proposes a consolidated application form for services such as DL renewal, issuance of duplicate licences, addition of a vehicle class and changes to personal particulars. articles.title: Why measles outbreak in Pennsylvania poses risks beyond US borders
articles.summary: The United States is facing its largest outbreak of measles since the virus was declared eliminated in 2000.
articles.body:
Decades after it was officially declared eliminated in the United States, measles has made a resurgence, with the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) announcing the third death of the year from the virus.

Matt Ferrari, director of Pennsylvania State University’s Center for Infectious Disease Dynamics, said the US was so successful at wiping out measles that it had “the luxury to forget” it was a serious problem.

“It’s been a long time, and for many of us in the United States, and in fact, throughout the Western Hemisphere, we have been able to forget how nasty measles is,” Ferrari told Al Jazeera.

Pennsylvania has been hit especially hard in the most recent outbreak. In September, the state sought emergency support from the CDC to control the spread, even as state and federal health officials quarrelled over the measles-associated death tally — differing over how deaths should be classified. State officials have recorded more than 1,200 cases and over 240 hospitalisations in 42 counties so far this year.

This spike in cases has raised concerns in neighbouring US states. On October 5, New York Governor Kathy Hochul declared a state disaster emergency in response to rising cases in rural areas, expanding the number of health professionals authorised to vaccinate and test people for measles.

“No one should get seriously ill or die from a vaccine-preventable disease,” Hochul said.

But experts warn that the risks extend far beyond US state borders. The US resurgence comes as measles cases increase globally , particularly in communities that are vaccine-sceptical or where there are gaps in healthcare access.

Vaccination coverage among US kindergartners has decreased from 95.2 percent during the 2019-2020 school year to 92.4 percent in the 2025-2026 school year. Experts warn that declining vaccination rates in one geographic location can leave people thousands of miles away vulnerable, making measles prevention a shared global responsibility.

Building trust in vaccine-sceptical communities

Pennsylvania reported in August that two unvaccinated people died of measles in Lancaster County, which is located in the South Central part of the state. Lancaster is considered the centre of Pennsylvania Dutch Country and home to the nation’s oldest Amish and Mennonite communities, both of which have under-vaccinated populations.

In Pennsylvania, public health officials have worked with community leaders to share information and expand access to vaccination. Joshua Good, principal of Ephrata Mennonite School in Lancaster County, where two students contracted measles earlier this year, worked with state officials to organise a pop-up vaccination clinic at the school.

He said officials also provided communication materials that the school adapted for its community and helped identify at-risk families.

While Good said the response was productive, he told state officials that the Mennonite community still holds a lot of vaccine scepticism.

“I said, look, if we do this, keep in mind, our community by and large…made that decision not because they don’t have access to the vaccines. They made the decision based on their own best judgement,” he told Al Jazeera.

Good, who is vaccinated and vaccinated his children, sees himself as an advocate within the community. If families have questions about measles shots, he will answer them as best he can.

“I have honest conversations with people, try to engage in respectful, charitable ways,” he said. “I’ll try to understand what their hesitancies are. That said, I respect their concerns.”

Although multiple community members received the measles vaccine at the Ephrata clinic, vaccination rates remain below the threshold for herd immunity.

Public health officials advocate for investing in robust community outreach before outbreaks happen.

“You can’t just show up in a community in an emergency– an emergency in which they might feel like you’re there to kind of blame them or shame them,” Jennifer Nuzzo, director of the Pandemic Center at the Brown University School of Public Health, told Al Jazeera. “You need to know them so that they see public health as a resource rather than law enforcement.”

She said low vaccination coverage and distrust of the government allow measles to spread even when vaccines are available. But that shouldn’t stop governments from building rapport with vaccine-sceptical communities.

“I worry that by framing it around their demographics, it lets governments off the hook in terms of what they’re supposed to be doing, which is stopping the spread of this dangerous disease,” Nuzzo said.

Experts explain that declining vaccination rates put not only these communities but also immunocompromised people at greater risk for disease. Herd immunity in the wider population formerly helped shield those most vulnerable to infection.

“Those are communities that have been at risk for years,” Ferrari said. “But higher rates of vaccination in the communities surrounding them offered a barrier.”

The continental Americas was the first World Health Organization (WHO) region to eliminate endemic measles transmission in 2016. Maintaining that status requires high and consistent vaccination coverage. The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) says coverage across the region remains below the target for both doses of the measles vaccine, contributing to noticeable consequences.

PAHO holds an annual RVC Measles Elimination Status Conference where an independent technical body of international experts monitors and reviews whether countries in the Americas have successfully eliminated measles, rubella, and congenital rubella syndrome. A country can lose its “elimination status” when the same measles virus genotype has circulated continuously for at least 12 months.

Last year, Canada became the first country in the continental Americas to lose its status after an outbreak that began in 2024. Some have warned that the US may be on track to lose its status this year.

But Dr Daniel Salas, executive manager of the Special Program for Comprehensive Immunisation at PAHO, told Al Jazeera that it’s not just the US that will be under review.

“We have Mexico, we have Bolivia that is going to be closely assessed because they could potentially lose status as well,” he said.

US Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr has repeatedly defended the US response to measles.

“We’re doing a better job than any country in the world at controlling the measles outbreak,” Kennedy said at an August 26 event in Florida. He cited higher case numbers in Mexico, Canada and Britain.

But Nuzzo said the repeated outbreaks across the US point to a country struggling to contain transmission.

“We have not seen it this bad,” she said. “It’s like this perpetual game of Whac-A-Mole. As long as there are vulnerable communities, as long as we don’t have strategies for early detection and rapid response and containment, measles will just keep on happening over and over and over again.”

Dr Salas told Al Jazeera that action within the first three days after a suspected case is critical, and health authorities should begin investigating and taking response measures without waiting for laboratory confirmation. Delays of a week or more can allow the highly contagious virus, marked by fever, coughing, and a whole-body rash, to spread further.

Experts warn that outbreaks cannot be treated as isolated local events. Scientific journals have found evidence that the virus strain in Canada’s latest measles outbreak was genetically linked to cases reported in US Mennonite communities. This was the same outbreak that resulted in Canada losing its measles elimination status.

“The spread of measles in the United States imperils other countries,” said Nuzzo. “It’s easy to kind of point to other countries and say that they’re the problem, but the reality is we’re all dependent on each other, and it’s very hard to protect ourselves when measles is spreading elsewhere.”
